questions.q: What question does the User and Role Access Audit Report answer?
options: What did this person actually do in the system
What access does this user or role actually have
How much does this user's job role cost to license
Which passwords have expired
questions.explain: The User and Role Access Audit Report shows function security privileges and, optionally, data security policies for a user or role — what access they actually hold.

questions.q: What must happen before the User and Role Access Audit Report can return meaningful results?
options: The user's password must be reset
All job roles must first be deleted and recreated
The Import User and Role Application Security Data process must be run to populate the underlying reporting tables
The report requires no setup at all
questions.explain: The report relies on data populated by the Import User and Role Application Security Data process; a stale or never-run import is a common cause of empty or incorrect results.

questions.q: What does Audit Trail track that the User and Role Access Audit Report does not?
options: A user's job title
The company's chart of accounts structure
Which browser a user signed in from
Actual create, update, and delete activity on enabled business objects, including before-and-after field values
questions.explain: Audit Trail is a detective control logging what a user actually did (transaction-level activity), as opposed to access reporting which shows what they are capable of doing.

questions.q: Why is reviewing the access audit report only once, right before go-live, considered insufficient?
options: Because it does not catch later drift, such as a role mapping over-provisioning access after a reorganization or a transferred employee keeping old access
Because the report can only be run one time ever
Because the report is only valid for 24 hours after go-live
Because Oracle requires it to be run only during implementation
questions.explain: Access drift happens over time as roles, mappings, and job assignments change, so recurring review (often quarterly) is needed to catch issues a one-time go-live check would miss.

questions.q: How do access reporting and audit trail complement each other when reviewing a suspicious transaction?
options: They are redundant and only one needs to be checked
Access reporting confirms the person had the access to perform the action, while audit trail confirms exactly what they changed
Audit trail replaces the need for any role-based security entirely
Access reporting only applies to Human Capital Management, never Financials
questions.explain: A thorough review typically uses both: access reporting establishes whether the person could have done it, and audit trail establishes what they actually did and changed.
